title: Celigo flow
description:
Fields for creating or updating a flow.

Use `pageProcessors` for simple linear flows or `routers` for conditional branching — never
include both. The `schedule` field uses Celigo's 6-field cron format (not standard 5-field).

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server requires a non-empty name on create and caps its length, but accepts an empty name on update; the spec requires a non-empty name on every write.

description.description: Free-text description of the flow's purpose.
examples: Synchronizes customer records from Salesforce to NetSuite every 15 minutes

x-celigo-canon.reason: Universal presence in stored docs is a UI-written default — the server accepts a minimal name-only flow without adding it.

_integrationId.description:
Integration this flow belongs to. Omitting it (or sending `null`) on
create no longer produces a standalone flow — the flow is auto-assigned
to the account's "Standalone flows" integration (or the create fails
with `422 standalone_flows_not_supported` when that integration is
missing). A value that is not a well-formed ObjectId is rejected with
`400 invalid_ref` rather than auto-assigned. Always set it explicitly.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: To move the flow to a different integration, PUT with a changed _integrationId AND remove _flowGroupingId (flow groups are per-integration; a stale value is rejected with 422 flowgrouping_not_belong). The platform registers the flow's step connections in the target integration on save.

Send a real integration id: a malformed value fails with 400 `invalid_ref`
("Please provide a valid _integrationId."), and a well-formed id that names
no integration in the account fails with 422 `invalid_ref`.

schedule.description:
Celigo 6-field cron expression: `? minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`.
Explicit minute/hour lists, ranges, wildcards, and step forms (`*/N`) are all valid.
Leave empty for event-driven or webhook-triggered flows. Validated on every
write, including while `disabled` is true, so a flow cannot be parked disabled
with a broken schedule: `422 invalid_value` when the expression cannot be parsed
into a schedule (for example all wildcards, `? * * ? * *`), `422
schedule_not_supported` when its runs would be less than a minute apart — which
is also what free text such as `every 5 minutes` produces.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Build `schedule` as a Celigo 6-field cron:
`? minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`.
The seconds field is always `?`; day-of-month is usually `?`, month `*`,
and day-of-week `*` (or specific days, 0=Sun..6=Sat).

Disabling a flow does not bypass schedule validation: POST, PUT, and PATCH
all reject free text or a sub-minute expression (`not a cron`, `* * * * * *`)
with 422 `schedule_not_supported`, and an expression that parses to no
schedule (`? * * ? * *`) with 422 `invalid_value`. Fix or clear the schedule
instead of disabling the flow to get past the error.

Prefer explicit lists when AUTHORING a schedule — hourly or longer:
minute `5` with an explicit hour list
(`? 5 0,4,8,12,16,20 ? * *` = every 4 hours;
`? 5 9 ? * 1,2,3,4,5` = weekdays 9 AM; `? 5 0 ? * *` = daily);
sub-hourly: an explicit minute list with hour `*`
(`? 0,15,30,45 * ? * *` = every 15 minutes). Lists match the UI's
schedule builder and make fire times unambiguous — the scheduler can
offset step expressions (the UI's sub-hourly presets fire at minutes
10/25/40/55).

Wildcard/step/range forms (`? */5 * * * *`, `? 10-59/30 * * * *`) are
valid and the scheduler runs them — never claim an existing schedule's
format is invalid or the cause of missed runs, and never rewrite a
working schedule into a different format as a fix. A new scheduled
instance is not started while a previous run of the flow is still in
progress (boundaries skipped during a long run are by design); missed
runs on an enabled, unchanged flow with nothing running are a
platform-scheduler issue to escalate, not a configuration problem.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the schedule (e.g. `America/New_York`). Defaults to UTC.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Open IANA timezone vocabulary — low observed cardinality is a population artifact, not a closed set.

disabled.description:
When true, scheduled executions are suspended and the flow cannot be triggered.
Running jobs are allowed to complete.

pageGenerators.description:
Data sources (exports) that produce pages of records for the flow. Mutually exclusive with
top-level `pageProcessors` when `routers` is used.

items.description:
A data source that produces pages of records for the flow. Page generators are the
entry points of a flow; each references an export, can carry its own schedule, and
multiple generators can run in parallel when the flow enables it.

_exportId.description:
Export that retrieves data from the source system. The server rejects page
generator entries without a valid export reference unless the entry is a
placeholder still being set up (`setupInProgress: true`).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The export defines:
- Connection to the source system
- Query or API configuration
- Data retrieval method (standard, delta, webhook, etc.)
- Pagination and filtering rules

schedule.description:
Cron expression for this specific generator, overriding the flow's main schedule.
When omitted, the generator inherits the flow's schedule.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When specified:
- Overrides the flow's main schedule for this generator
- Allows different data sources to refresh at different intervals
- Useful for sources with varying update frequencies

skipRetries.description:
When true, failed records from this generator are not retried — errors are logged
and the flow continues. When false (the default), failed records are retried per
platform policy.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When true:
- Failed attempts are not retried
- Errors are logged but flow may continue
- Useful for non-critical or time-sensitive data

setupInProgress.description: When true, the generator's configuration is still being set up in the UI and the step is not yet runnable.

_keepDeltaBehindFlowId.description:
Coordinates delta timing so this generator's checkpoint stays behind the referenced
flow, preventing child records from being processed before their parents.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When specified:
- This generator's delta timestamp stays behind the referenced flow
- Prevents processing child records before parent records
- Maintains referential integrity across flows

_keepDeltaBehindExportId.description: Like `_keepDeltaBehindFlowId` but targets a specific export's delta timestamp.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
More granular than _keepDeltaBehindFlowId:
- Targets a specific export's delta timestamp
- Provides precise control over data dependencies
- Useful for complex multi-source synchronization

__startDateHelper.description:
Server-managed scheduling bookkeeping written by the platform when a run
starts. Never send it: the API silently drops any client-supplied value.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Page generators are the entry points of a flow that retrieve data from source systems.
They can be scheduled independently or inherit the flow's schedule, and multiple generators
can run in parallel if configured.

pageProcessors.description:
Sequential processing steps (imports, lookups, routers). Mutually exclusive with `routers` —
use one or the other, not both.

items.description:
A processing step that operates on pages of records within a flow. Processors are
either lookups (`type: export`) that enrich records or imports (`type: import`) that
write records to a destination, and execute sequentially unless routed into branches.

type.description: Selects whether this step runs a lookup export or an import, and which reference field applies.

x-enumDescriptions.export: Uses an export resource (configured as a lookup) for data lookup or enrichment.
x-enumDescriptions.import: Uses an import resource to send data to a destination system.

_exportId.description:
Lookup export that enriches incoming records. Required when `type` is `export`;
the referenced export must be configured as a lookup (`isLookup: true`).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Required when type="export". The export must be configured as a lookup
(isLookup=true) to receive and process incoming records.

Common uses:
- Retrieve additional details from a system
- Validate data against a reference source
- Enrich records with related information

_importId.description: Import that writes records to the destination system. Required when `type` is `import`.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Required when type="import". The import defines:
- Target system connection
- Data mapping and transformation
- Error handling and validation rules
- Create/update logic

proceedOnFailure.description:
When true, records that fail in this processor continue to subsequent steps and the
error is logged. When false, failed records stop at this step.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When true:
- Errors are logged but don't stop the flow
- Subsequent processors continue execution
- Failed records may be skipped

responseMapping.description:
Merges fields from a step's response back onto the in-flight record so
downstream steps can read them. Applies to both lookup steps
(`type: "export"`) and import steps (`type: "import"`); without it, the
step's response is discarded after the call.

`fields` and `lists` are plain arrays — exactly the shape GET returns.

Extract paths do NOT read the raw application response — the platform
wraps every response in a canonical per-record envelope first, and
extracts evaluate against that envelope:

- **Lookup steps**: `{"statusCode": 200, "data": [<result records>],
  "errors": []}` — `data` holds the records the lookup returned, so
  extracts must start from it: `data[0].name` copies a field of the
  first result, `data` copies the whole result array. A bare
  result-record field name (e.g. `name`) resolves to nothing and merges
  nothing.
- **Import steps**: `{"id": "<destination record id>", "statusCode": 200,
  "ignored": false, "errors": [], "_json": <raw destination response>}` —
  use `id` for the destination-assigned id and `_json.<path>` for fields
  inside the destination's response body. The full envelope (including
  `id`) is present on real runs and in flow-builder previews; flow TEST
  runs never execute imports, and their mock-built envelope carries no
  `id` — an `extract: "id"` merges nothing in a test run even though it
  works on real runs.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Send `fields` and `lists` as bare arrays, exactly as GET returns them.
Never wrap either in an object (e.g. `"fields": {"type": [...]}`): the
API does not reject that shape — it returns 200 and silently persists
`fields: [null]` / `lists: [{"fields": []}]`, erasing the step's
response mappings.

responseMapping is fully replaced on PUT: omitting it resets the step
to empty `{"fields": [], "lists": []}`. Always send the complete
intended mapping for every step.

To carry several lookup results onto the record, use `extract: "data"`
(the whole result array) or a `lists` entry whose extracts use
`data[*].x` — never `data[*].x` in `fields[].extract`, which merges
nothing: the record simply never gains the field.

fields.description:
Field mappings that copy individual values from the response
envelope onto the in-flight record.

extract.description:
Path within the canonical response envelope to copy the value
from. For lookup steps, paths start from the envelope's `data`
array (`data[0].x` and `data.0.x` are equivalent; `data` alone
copies every result); for import steps, use the envelope fields
`id`, `statusCode`, `ignored`, or `_json.<path>` for the raw
response body. Paths that skip the envelope (bare response
field names) resolve to nothing, and a `[*]` wildcard is not
honored here — `data[*].x` merges nothing; iterate arrays with
`lists` instead.

generate.description:
Field path on the in-flight record where the extracted value
is stored, using dot notation for nesting. Downstream steps
read the value at this path.

lists.description:
Array mappings that build a target array on the in-flight record
from an array inside the response envelope — one output item per
element of the array the item extracts mark with `[*]` (`data[*].x`
for lookups, `_json.<arrayPath>[*].x` for imports); an empty source
array yields an empty target array. Not needed for one-to-many
(fan-out) merge-back, which uses plain field mappings.

generate.description:
Array field created on the in-flight record to hold the
mapped items.

fields.description:
Field mappings applied to each item of the source array to
produce the corresponding target-array item.

extract.description:
Full envelope path to the source value, with `[*]`
marking the array to iterate — `data[*].productId` for a
lookup, `_json.items[*].sku` for an import. A path without
`[*]` (e.g. `statusCode`) repeats the same envelope value
on every item; an item-relative name (`productId`)
resolves to nothing and produces empty objects.

generate.description: Target field within each mapped array item.

hooks.description: Custom code hooks extending this processor's behavior.

postResponseMap.description: Hook that runs after the step's response mapping completes.

function.description: Function to invoke within the referenced script.

_scriptId.description: Script containing the hook function named in `function`.

setupInProgress.description: When true, the processor's configuration is still being set up in the UI and the step is not yet runnable.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Page processors can be exports (for lookups), imports (for data loading), or references
to routers for conditional processing. They execute sequentially unless part of a router branch.

routers.description:
Routing configurations that direct records to conditional branches. Mutually exclusive with
top-level `pageProcessors` — use one or the other, not both.

items.description:
Configuration for conditional routing that directs records to different processing branches.

Routers evaluate each record against defined criteria and route them to appropriate branches
for specialized processing. This enables complex business logic and conditional workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this router within the flow.

Used to reference this router from branches (`branches[].nextRouterId`)
when chaining routers. Must be unique within the flow's router collection.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the router.

Displayed in the UI and logs to help identify the router's purpose.

routeRecordsTo.description: Strategy for routing records to branches.

x-enumDescriptions.first_matching_branch: Routes each record to only the first branch whose criteria match.
x-enumDescriptions.all_matching_branches: Routes each record to every branch whose criteria match, creating copies.

routeRecordsUsing.description: Method used to evaluate routing criteria.

x-enumDescriptions.input_filters: Evaluate routing criteria using declarative filter expressions.
x-enumDescriptions.script: Evaluate routing criteria using a custom JavaScript function.

script.description:
Script configuration when routeRecordsUsing="script".

Enables custom routing logic that can't be expressed with filters.

function.description: Function name that returns the branch name for each record

branches.description:
List of branches that define different processing paths.

Each branch has its own criteria and processing steps. Records are evaluated
against branch criteria in the order defined.

items.description:
Configuration for a single branch within a router that defines criteria and processing steps.

Each branch represents a conditional path that records can take based on matching criteria.
Branches are evaluated in order, and records are routed based on the router's strategy.

name.description:
Unique name for this branch within the router.

Used for:
- Identification in logs and monitoring
- Reference in custom routing scripts
- Display in the UI

Should be descriptive of the branch's purpose or criteria.

description.description:
Optional description explaining the branch's purpose and criteria.

Helps document:
- What types of records this branch handles
- Business logic or rules applied
- Why this branch exists
examples: Handles enterprise customers with annual revenue > $1M

inputFilter.description:
Filter criteria that determines which records match this branch.

Only used when the router's routeRecordsUsing="inputFilter".
Records matching these criteria will be routed to this branch.

version.description: Version of the filter expression language

rules.description:
Filter expression array defining the matching criteria, in the platform's
prefix-notation filter DSL: the first element is an operator name and the
remaining elements are its operands, which may themselves be nested
expression arrays.

```
[operator, operand1, operand2, ...]
```

Uses the same expression language as export/import filters
(`Filter.expression.rules`): comparison operators (`equals`, `notequals`,
`greaterthan`, `lessthan`, `startswith`, `contains`, `isempty`, `matches`, ...),
logical operators (`and`, `or`, `not`), field access (`extract`, `settings`)
and type conversions (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `epochtime`).

Example — route records whose `isDeleted` field is the string "false":
```json
["equals", ["string", ["extract", "isDeleted"]], "false"]
```

pageProcessors.description:
List of processors that execute for records routed to this branch.

These processors:
- Execute in sequence for records matching this branch
- Can include exports, imports, or nested routers
- Have the same structure as flow-level page processors
- Continue until completion or error (unless proceedOnFailure is set)

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server accepts a bare name-only branch and normalizes pageProcessors to an empty array — universal production presence is server-fill, not a client requirement.

nextRouterId.description:
Chains this branch to another router: after the branch's pageProcessors
complete, records continue to the router whose `id` matches this value.

Enables sequential routing decisions where records pass through multiple
routers for complex branching logic. The server validates the reference —
a value that does not match any router `id` in the flow is rejected with
a 422 ("Invalid nextRouterId is defined on the branch").

branchId.description:
Stable identifier for this branch, used to correlate branch-level state
(for example dashboards and error reporting) across saves. Generated by
the server when omitted; a client-supplied value is kept as-is.

_exportId.description:
Source export of a simple (single source, single destination) flow — the legacy
pre-flow-builder model still produced by Data Loader flows. Paired with `_importId`
instead of `pageGenerators`/`pageProcessors`; the server accepts and serves both
forms. Prefer `pageGenerators` for new flows.

_importId.description:
Destination import of a simple (single source, single destination) flow — the legacy
pre-flow-builder model still produced by Data Loader flows. Paired with `_exportId`
instead of `pageGenerators`/`pageProcessors`. Prefer `pageProcessors` for new flows.

_runNextFlowIds.description:
Flow IDs to trigger after this flow completes successfully. Accepts null as
equivalent to an empty list (the server also serves null on documents saved
that way).

x-celigo-canon.reason: Universal presence in stored docs is a UI-written default — the server accepts a minimal name-only flow without adding it.

_runNextExportIds.description: Specific exports in other flows to trigger after completion.

_flowId.description: Flow containing the export to trigger.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Universal presence in stored docs is a UI-written default — the server accepts a minimal name-only flow without adding it.

externalId.description: External identifier for correlating the flow with a record in another system.

x-enumDescriptions.step2: The flow setup wizard is on its second step.
x-enumDescriptions.step3: The flow setup wizard is on its third step.
x-enumDescriptions.done: The flow setup wizard has been completed.

wizardState.description: Tracks how far the user has progressed through the flow setup wizard in the UI.

settings.description:
Custom key-value settings for this flow. At runtime the flow's steps read them
under the fixed scope key `flow` — e.g. the Handlebars expression
`{{settings.flow.batchSize}}`, the Mapper 2.0 envelope path
`$.settings.flow.batchSize`, or `options.settings.flow` in script hooks.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user/integrator payload — interiors deliberately unconstrained per the campaign rule; do not model keys.

runPageGeneratorsInParallel.description: When true, all page generators start simultaneously instead of sequentially.

autoResolveMatchingTraceKeys.description:
When true, a new error for a record whose trace key already has open errors on the same step
auto-resolves the older ones, a later success for that record auto-resolves its open errors,
and errors classified `intermittent` are retried automatically — up to four attempts, the
first about 30 minutes after the error.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Both behaviors hang off this one flag — off means repeated failures of a record stay open and intermittent errors get no automatic retries; never turn it off as a fix for "duplicate" errors (those come from the destination, not from trace keys).
Intermittent auto-retry does not depend on the trace key — errors with a blank trace key are scheduled and retried the same way; a blank key only loses the duplicate collapse.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The server stamps true on every create that omits it (integration-scoped creates included), so a request never needs to send it — the stored value is a server default, not a UI artifact.

isAbstract.description:
Marks this as an abstract (multi-instance) flow — a reusable template that cannot be
executed directly. Instance flows reference it via `_abstractFlowId` and provide `overrides`.

Constraints: top-level `pageProcessors` are not allowed (use `routers`), cannot reference
another abstract flow, cannot be a "run next" target, and cannot be unset while instances exist.

_abstractFlowId.description:
Abstract flow this instance inherits from. Immutable once set. The instance inherits
the flow graph and uses `overrides` to customize connections, schedules, and hooks.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When `_abstractFlowId` is set the flow is an instance:
customize it only through `overrides`.
Do not set `pageGenerators`, `pageProcessors`, `routers`,
or `runPageGeneratorsInParallel` on the instance — they are inherited from the abstract flow.

overrides.description:
Configuration overrides for flows that inherit from abstract flows.

When a flow inherits from an abstract flow template, this object allows selective
overriding of inherited configuration while maintaining the base structure.

name.description: Override for the flow's display name

examples: Production version of the customer sync template

settings.description:
Override for custom flow settings.

Allows modifying specific settings while inheriting others from
the abstract flow template.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user/integrator payload — interiors deliberately unconstrained per the campaign rule; do not model keys.

timezone.description: Override for the flow's schedule timezone

_runNextFlowIds.description: Override list of flows to trigger after completion

_runNextExportIds.description: Override list of exports to trigger after completion

__listenerIdsToIndex.description:
Server-managed listener index auto-populated by the platform on instance
flows. Never send it as part of a request.

connections.description:
Override connection configurations for abstract flow connections.

Maps abstract connection placeholders to concrete connection instances.

_abstractId.description: ID of the abstract connection being overridden

_id.description: Concrete connection ID to use instead

_borrowConcurrencyFromConnectionId.description:
Optional connection to share concurrency limits with.

Useful when multiple connections access the same system
and need to share rate limiting.

exports.description:
Override configurations for exports in the abstract flow.

Allows customizing export behavior while maintaining the flow structure.

_abstractId.description: ID of the abstract export being overridden

_id.description: Concrete export ID to use (if replacing entirely)

_connectionId.description: Override the connection used by this export

schedule.description:
Replaces the page generator's schedule for this instance, in the same
Celigo 6-field cron format as the flow-level `schedule`. Parsed on every
write regardless of `disabled`; an unparseable expression fails with
`422 invalid_value` at `overrides.exports[i].schedule`.

mappings.description: Overrides the Mapper 2.0 field mappings on the abstract flow's export (lookup step), which reshape records the lookup returns.

pageSize.description: Override page size for this export

dataURITemplate.description: Override URI template for error tracking

version.description: Version of the filter expression format used by the rules; currently only "1" is supported.

rules.description: Filter expression defining the matching criteria, in prefix notation — the operator first, followed by its operands, which may be nested expressions.

limit.description: Overrides the test-mode record cap on the abstract flow's export — the total number of records a test run processes.

dateField.description: Overrides the delta date field on the abstract flow's export — the record timestamp field(s) compared against the last successful run time to identify changed records. Accepts a single field or multiple comma-separated fields.

dateFormat.description: Overrides the moment.js format string applied to the delta cutoff timestamp; ISO 8601 is used when unset.

startDate.description: Overrides the fixed start timestamp used for the delta window on the abstract flow's export, in place of the last successful run time.

lagOffset.description: Overrides the buffer in milliseconds subtracted from the last successful run timestamp, creating an overlapping window that catches late-propagating records.

endDateField.description: Overrides the record timestamp field used as the upper bound of the delta window on the abstract flow's export.

booleanField.description: Overrides the once-mode tracking field on the abstract flow's export — the boolean field in the source system that is false for unprocessed records and set to true after successful processing.

exportedField.description: Overrides the field that tracks the last exported value on the abstract flow's export.

pendingField.description: Overrides the field that tracks the pending (not yet exported) value on the abstract flow's export.

token_crypt.description: Encrypted form of the webhook verification token, stored at rest.

token_salt.description: Salt used to encrypt the corresponding webhook token.

path.description: Overrides the location of the verification token on the abstract flow's webhook export — a JSON path into the request body or a query parameter name.

key_crypt.description: Encrypted form of the webhook HMAC or public key, stored at rest.

key_salt.description: Salt used to encrypt the corresponding webhook key.

header.description: Overrides the name of the request header that carries the HMAC signature on the abstract flow's webhook export.

username.description: Overrides the username used for basic-auth webhook verification on the abstract flow's export.

password_crypt.description: Encrypted form of the basic-auth webhook password, stored at rest.

password_salt.description: Salt used to encrypt the corresponding webhook password.

successStatusCode.description: Overrides the HTTP status code returned to the webhook caller after successful processing.

successBody.description: Overrides the response body returned to the webhook caller after successful processing; ignored when the status code is 204.

successMediaType.description: Overrides the Content-Type of successful webhook responses; must match the format of the success body.

bearerToken_crypt.description: Encrypted form of the distributed export's bearer token, stored at rest.

bearerToken_salt.description: Salt used to encrypt the corresponding bearer token.

imports.description:
Override configurations for imports in the abstract flow.

Similar structure to export overrides but for import resources.

_abstractId.description: ID of the abstract import being overridden

_connectionId.description: Override the connection used by this import

idLockTemplate.description: Overrides the ID lock template on the abstract flow's import — a handlebars template that generates a lock key so records resolving to the same key are not submitted concurrently.

dataURITemplate.description: Overrides the data URI template on the abstract flow's import — a handlebars template that builds a link back to each record in the destination application's UI for error tracking.

pathToMany.description: Overrides the one-to-many path on the abstract flow's import — the JSON path to child records within each parent record.

blobKeyPath.description: Overrides the blob key path on the abstract flow's import — the path in the input record that holds the blob key identifying file content to import.

filter.description: Overrides the filter on the abstract flow's import, which selects which incoming records are sent to the destination system.

traceKeyTemplate.description: Overrides the trace key template on the abstract flow's import — a handlebars template controlling how each record's unique trace key is generated.

parsers.description: Overrides the parser configurations on the abstract flow's import.

hooks.description: Overrides the hook configurations on the abstract flow's import — custom JavaScript hooks that run at fixed points in the import lifecycle.

responseTransform.description: Overrides the response transform on the abstract flow's import, which reshapes the destination system's response after records are imported.

mapping.description: Overrides the Mapper 1.0 mapping configuration on the abstract flow's import.

mappings.description: Overrides the Mapper 2.0 field mappings on the abstract flow's import, which transform incoming records into the destination system's field structure.

lookups.description: Overrides the lookup definitions on the abstract flow's import, referenced by its field mappings.

settingsForm.description: Overrides the settings form definition on the abstract flow's import, which prompts users for values stored in `settings`.

preSave.description: Overrides the preSave hook on the abstract flow's import — a JavaScript hook that executes before the resource is saved.

settings.description: Overrides the custom settings on the abstract flow's import, accessible to hooks, filters, mappings, and handlebars templates at runtime.

routers.description:
Override configurations for routers in the abstract flow.

Allows customizing router behavior and branch configurations.

_abstractId.description: ID of the abstract router being overridden

_scriptId.description: Reference to the script resource containing the routing logic used in place of the abstract router's script.

function.description: Function name within the script that returns the branch name for each record.

_abstractId.description: ID of the abstract branch being overridden

name.description: Overrides the branch's display name within the router.

description.description: Overrides the branch's description explaining its purpose and criteria.

inputFilter.description: Overrides the branch's input filter — the criteria that determine which records are routed to this branch.

version.description: Version of the filter expression format used by the rules; currently only "1" is supported.

rules.description: Filter expression defining the branch's matching criteria, in prefix notation — the operator first, followed by its operands.

overridesHelper.description:
Metadata for abstract flows that declares which fields in the flow's connections,
exports, imports, and routers are overridable by instance flows.

Only valid on abstract flows (isAbstract: true). The backend rejects this field
on non-abstract flows. Each entry references a component of the abstract flow by
its ID and lists the field names that instance flows are allowed to override.

fields.description: Flow-level field names that instance flows may override (e.g., "schedule", "timezone")

connections.description: Declares which connection-level fields are overridable per abstract flow connection.

_abstractId.description: ID of the connection in the abstract flow

fields.description: Field names on this connection that instance flows may override

_flowGroupingId.description:
Flow grouping for organizing related flows in the UI. References an entry in the
integration's `flowGroupings` array (not a standalone collection); invalid ids are
silently dropped by the server. At runtime the flow's steps read the referenced
group's `settings` under the fixed scope key `flowGrouping` (e.g.
`{{settings.flowGrouping.<fieldId>}}`).

_keepDeltaBehindFlowId.description:
Coordinates delta timing so this flow's checkpoint stays behind the referenced flow.
Used for parent-child data relationships where the parent must sync first.

_keepDeltaBehindExportId.description: Like `_keepDeltaBehindFlowId` but targets a specific export within a flow.

aiDescription.description:
AI-generated descriptions and documentation for the resource.

This object contains automatically generated content that helps users
understand the purpose, behavior, and configuration of the resource without
requiring them to analyze the technical details. The AI-generated content
is sanitized and safe for display in the UI.

summary.description:
Brief AI-generated summary of the resource's purpose and functionality.

This concise description provides a quick overview of what the resource does,
what systems it interacts with, and its primary role in the integration.
The summary is suitable for display in list views, dashboards, and other
contexts where space is limited.

Maximum length: 10KB
examples: AI-generated overview of what this resource does and the systems it interacts with.

detailed.description:
Comprehensive AI-generated description of the resource's functionality.

This detailed explanation covers the resource's purpose, configuration details,
data flow patterns, filtering logic, and other technical aspects. It provides
in-depth information suitable for documentation, tooltips, or detailed views
in the administration interface.

The content may include HTML formatting for improved readability.

Maximum length: 10KB
examples:
A detailed AI-generated explanation of this resource's purpose, configuration, and behavior.

The text is regenerated when the resource's configuration changes.

generatedOn.description:
Timestamp indicating when the AI description was generated.

This field helps track the freshness of the AI-generated content and
determine when it might need to be regenerated due to changes in the
resource's configuration or behavior.

The timestamp is recorded in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (Z suffix).

aliases.description: Named aliases that map to specific resources within the flow.

draft.description:
When true, this flow is a draft that auto-deletes when its expiry passes
(`draftExpiresAt` in the response). Set at creation; an update can clear the
flag but never set it.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
POST with `draft: true` arms the draft TTL (the server computes `draftExpiresAt`).
PUT with `draft: false` clears the flag and the expiry, promoting the draft to a
permanent flow. PUT with `draft: true` on a non-draft flow is silently ignored,
and a PUT that omits the field leaves an existing draft flag unchanged.

sandbox.description:
When true, the flow is created in the account's sandbox environment.
Honored on create only.

preSave.description: Pre-save hook that runs a script before persisting flow changes.

settingsForm.description: Form definition for collecting flow-level settings from users in the UI.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user/integrator payload — interiors deliberately unconstrained per the campaign rule; do not model keys.
